title: Streaming handshake race, eager KV commit, and graceful degradation roadmap
creator: Priya Shah
description: After the 2025-02-10 capacity surge, several customer sessions experienced mid-stream disconnects with truncated or duplicated token output. Initial triage shows a race between the streaming connection handshake (reconnect path) and an eager KV-cache commit path that frees session state before the client has fully resumed, causing partial-token delivery and backpressure signals to be lost. This ticket tracks the incident follow-ups, short-term mitigations, and long-term fixes to eliminate the handshake/commit race and provide graceful degradation when capacity is constrained.
impact_summary: ~3.2% of streaming sessions in eu-west-1 during the 12:21–12:48 UTC window saw either partial token sequences or reconnect-triggered duplication. Affected customers included medium-traffic tenants on Dedicated and several Hosted API customers with long-lived chat sessions. Business impact: increased error rates and user-visible truncation for some production workloads.
updates: 2025-02-15: Ticket created by Priya after postmortem sync. Initial hypothesis: session state freed early due to eager commit on unlock path.
2025-02-16: Traced 84 session timelines where reconnects aligned with KV commit calls; reproduced locally by forcing a disconnect immediately after commit path executes (repo test harness).

2025-02-18: Deployed emergency mitigation: extend handshake grace window from 500ms->1500ms behind feature flag (ff/streaming/handshake-grace-1500). Observed reduction of partial-token incidents to 0.4% in canary zone (10% traffic).
2025-02-20: Opened PRs: infra PR github.com/redwood/infra/pull/12412 (grace-window feature-flag), runtime PR github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/9814 (handshake telemetry).

2025-02-24: Root-cause confirmed: ordering bug where eager KV commit path calls session_free() before handshake ack; race window widened under high queue pressure and aggressive batching. Also found backpressure signals dropped when session metadata removed mid-retry loop.

2025-03-01: Design doc published (drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3C_handshake-commit-design). Long-term plan approved: atomic commit marker, explicit handshake-ack protocol, rework of session lifecycle to make commit idempotent and observable.
2025-03-03: Implementation of atomic commit marker (runtime PR github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/10023) merged to canary; rollback plan and canary rollout scheduled for 2025-03-05.
2025-03-03: Post-release items: add session-state timeline view in Console, fuzz tests for handshake+disconnect races, and run chaos experiments simulating connection churn at 200% historical peak.
acceptance_criteria: Handshake race eliminated: no observed partial-token incidents in canary for 48h at simulated peak load
KV commit becomes atomic marker: session state not freed until handshake-ack observed or a deterministic timeout that logs an explicit commit failure
Backpressure signals preserved across reconnects: add telemetry showing pressure metrics continuity across reconnects
Dashboard: new Console view showing per-session lifecycle timeline and commit/ack events
E2E test coverage: fuzzing harness that reproduces handshake-commit races included in CI; test passes consistently
action_items: ENG: runtime change - introduce atomic commit marker and delay session_free until ack or logged timeout (owner: Liam O'Connor, estimate: 3)
ENG: infra - expose feature flag and canary routing for handshake grace window and schedule 5%->25%->100% rollout (owner: Marco Rivera, estimate: 2)
ENG: observability - implement session timeline traces and add commit/ack span tags (owner: Mei Chen, estimate: 2)
ENG: qa - add fuzz tests that simulate reconnection during commit with variable network jitter and load (owner: Diego Alvarez, estimate: 2)
PM: customer comms - draft targeted postmortem and mitigation notes for impacted tenants (owner: Aisha Malik, estimate: 1)
ENG: resilience - add circuit-breaker guard to prevent eager commit when queue length > threshold and fail open with graceful degradation path (owner: Priya Shah, estimate: 3)
ENG: monitoring - add SLO alert for partial-token ratio > 0.1% and create dashboard panel (owner: Sunita Rao, estimate: 1)
SEC: review - confirm no new data-exposure risk with changed commit/ack protocol (owner: Joel Park, estimate: 1)
ENG: rollout - canary plan and rollback steps documented with test checklist (owner: Marco Rivera, estimate: 1)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Extending grace window may increase resource retention and memory pressure under sustained churn. Mitigation: gated feature flag with autoscaler policy and backpressure threshold to limit retention per node.

Risk: Changing session lifecycle may introduce regressions in older Dedicated runtimes. Mitigation: offer a compatibility toggle and staged upgrade with telemetry to compare behavior between old/new runtimes.
Risk: Observability gaps could hide regressions. Mitigation: instrument commit/ack paths immediately and require a green signal from canary before ramping traffic.
